project.title: TrackMe Fitness
project.summary: An offline-first full-stack mobile workout tracker: Tauri + React client, Axum + Postgres server, custom background sync engine. Unifies lifting + running. Repo is private for now.

sections.title: Overview
sections.body: TrackMe Fitness is an offline-first mobile workout tracker that unifies lifting and running in a single app. Built solo as a deliberate deep dive into Rust, async Rust, the Tauri ecosystem, and designing a real client/server system from the ground up.

sections.title: Architecture
sections.body:
Client (Tauri mobile app): React + MUI webview, Rust Tauri commands own all HTTP/sync logic, local SQLite database, background sync worker (tokio interval + Notify).

Server (Rust): Axum REST API with Tower middleware (CORS, tracing), JWT extractor + Argon2 login, Postgres via sqlx.

Key idea: The webview never talks to the network. UI only invokes Rust commands; Rust owns all HTTP, token handling, and sync. Security-sensitive logic stays in typed, testable Rust.

sections.title: Planning
sections.body:
Development followed deliberate complexity sequencing across 8 phases:
1. Client prototype — UI + data modeling only
2. Local persistence — SQLite + data model (prove offline works)
3. Backend + Sync — Axum + Postgres + batched push/pull (no auth)
4. Local integration — Docker Postgres + native server
5. Temporary Auth — JWT extractor + temp token endpoint (prove isolation)
6. Real Login — Argon2 /auth/login, demo accounts
7. Sign-out + Polish — wipe local data, immediate sync, cycle signaling
8. Mobile + Deploy — phone build, Render deploy, multi-account test

Each phase isolated variables so failures had a single cause.

sections.title: Demo
sections.body: Repository is private (possible future monetization). Screenshots in the project page demonstrate the running application. Deployed backend runs on Render under a custom subdomain; mobile app builds and runs on physical devices against it.
